title: 2 Chronicles 1
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon son of David established himself firmly in his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great. ² Solomon spoke to all Israel — to the commanders of thousands and hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader and head of family throughout Israel. ³ Then Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, for that was where the tent of meeting stood — the tabernacle that Moses the LORD's servant had built in the wilderness. ⁴ David had already brought the ark of God up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, having pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem. ⁵ The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made stood before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly went there to seek God.

⁶ Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it. ⁷ That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you." ⁸ Solomon answered God, "You showed great kindness to my father David and have made me king in his place. ⁹ Now, LORD God, let your promise to my father David hold true, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth. ¹⁰ Give me wisdom and knowledge so that I may lead this people — for who could possibly govern this great nation of yours?"

¹¹ God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart — because you did not ask for wealth, riches, or honor, and you did not ask for the death of your enemies or for a long life, but instead asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people over whom I have made you king — ¹² wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. And I will also give you wealth, riches, and honor beyond anything any king before you has ever had, and no king after you will match it." ¹³ Solomon returned from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, and went to Jerusalem, where he reigned over Israel. ¹⁴ He gathered chariots and horsemen — fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen — and stationed them in the chariot cities and with himself in Jerusalem. ¹⁵ The king made silver and gold as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as common as the fig trees in the foothills.

¹⁶ Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt, and his merchants bought linen yarn at a set price. ¹⁷ They would acquire a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty — and in this way they also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
